subject: Post-call: MediLogic log handling & redaction options (next steps)
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@medilogic.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Jul 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: MediLogic log handling & redaction options (next steps)

Alice — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we’re aligned.

Call highlights (30 min):
- Scope: PoC to validate that request/response logging can be collected for troubleshooting while removing any PII and limiting trace identifiers for telemetry.
- Requirements you called out: no raw PII in logs, 90-day retention for sanitized audit stream, logs stored in us-east-1, and an ingestion-time scrub for certain headers (Authorization, Cookie, X-User-Email).
- Risk signal: your security team wants an auditable mapping of what’s redacted vs hashed vs dropped.

Proposed approach (options for your team to pick):
1) Strict redact at ingest — remove full header/value pairs and replace with stable hash for correlation (recommended for strict compliance).
2) Prefix-strip trace IDs — keep token length/presence but strip the variable suffix (lower entropy) so traces remain linkable but not reversible.
3) Sample & retain ephemeral KV cache for 7 days — store minimal routing metadata for debugging, then expire.

Ask from you:
- Confirm which approach (1/2/3) you prefer for the PoC.
- Provide the security contact who will accept the evidence package (SOC2 + architecture diagram).
- Confirm the list of headers/fields to treat as sensitive (we captured: Authorization, Cookie, X-User-Email, X-Trace-Token).

Deliverables we’ll send after you confirm:
- One-pager on logging controls (attached).
- Example sanitized log samples for your review.
- PoC kickoff agenda and timeline (targeting 2-week PoC).

Attachments: redwood-logging-controls-onepager.pdf (one-pager), sample PoC plan link.

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm approach and security contact by EOD Thu July 14.
- We schedule a 45-min technical kickoff next week (Ben to lead engineering scope).

Thanks —
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Post-call: MediLogic log handling & redaction options (next steps)

Rachel — thanks for the clear recap. A couple of clarifications from our side: we are leaning toward option 2 (prefix-strip trace IDs) combined with hashing for user-identifiers. Two asks from Security: 1) Can you show a sample of a redacted request/response pair (we want to validate the anonymization), and 2) we need an evidence bundle: SOC2 report, data flow diagram that highlights where logs are persisted, and a short note on retention controls.

Two notes:
- Storage must be in us-east-1 (we cannot accept outside-region logs).
- Retention: 90 days for sanitized logs, 7 days for any un-sanitized caches.

I’m looping in security@medilogic.com — they’ll review the sample. Once they sign off we can confirm the PoC.

Alice
Alice Gomez

On Tue, Jul 12, 2028 at 12:43 PM Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@medilogic.com> wrote:
> Rachel — thanks for the clear recap. A couple of clarifications from our side: we are leaning toward option 2 (prefix-strip trace IDs) combined with hashing for user-identifiers.

Thanks Alice — quick technical note from engineering:
- Prefix-strip approach: we can implement a deterministic prefix stripper that keeps the first N chars of a trace token and zeroes the rest. That preserves basic span ordering while making values non-reversible. N=8 is typical; we can tune.
- Hashing user-identifiers: we recommend HMAC-SHA256 with a customer-provided key (KMS/HSM optional) so MediLogic controls determinism across retries without Redwood being able to reverse.
- Implementation timeline: we can deliver an ingestion hook + sanitized sample logs within 3 business days after you confirm the approach. Full PoC (integration, verification, evidence handoff) ~10 business days.

Attached: draft test vector (we’ll generate synthetic request/response pairs) and an evidence checklist we’ll use for your security team.

Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: mds-requested-evidence.zip (contains evidence checklist, draft sanitized samples)
